Rashi on Arakhin 17a:12:1.hebrew: אומר אני אף בערכין כן - אילו מתרמי בערכין דומיא דקרבנות, הוי כקרבנות. דהא דאמרת דערכין אינן כקרבנות, משום דלא דמו אהדדי. דמפני מה עני שהעריך עשיר נותן ערך עני לפי השג ידו? משום דאין העשיר חייב כלום, ולא דמי למצורע. וזה שאמר על העשיר, לא נתכוון אלא לפי מדת שנותיו של העשיר — שפחותין או יתירין על שנותיו שלו. הלכך, נידון בהשג יד, דהא לא פירש כלום, אלא ערך מדת [שנותיו של] העשיר קיבל עליו, ודין ערך נידון בהשג יד:
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:12:1.english: I say: Even with regard to valuations [it is] so - If it happens in [the case of] valuations in a manner similar to offerings, it is like offerings. For that which you said, that valuations are not like offerings, [is] because they are not similar to one another: For why does a poor person who valuated a wealthy person give the valuation of a poor person according to his means? Because the wealthy person is not obligated in anything, and [thus] it is not similar to a leper. And this [person] who spoke regarding the wealthy person intended only according to the measure of the wealthy person's years — which are fewer or greater than his own years. Therefore, he is judged according to [his] means, for he did not specify anything [further]; rather, he accepted upon himself the valuation of the measure of [the years of] the wealthy person, and the law of valuation is judged according to [one's] means.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:12:2.hebrew: אבל עשיר שאמר ערכי עלי - דהוי חייב ערך שלם, דומיא דמצורע עשיר, ושמע עני וכו':
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:12:2.english: But a wealthy person who said: "My valuation is upon me" - For he is obligated [to pay] a full valuation, similar to a wealthy leper, and a poor person heard, etc.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:13:1.hebrew: וקפריך השג יד במעריך הוא - ולא בנודר, שהאומר דמי עלי אין נידון בהשג יד, אלא הכל יתן כשיוכל. דאמרינן בפרק האומר משקלי עלי (לקמן ערכין כ.): חומר בנדרים מבערכין, שהנדרים אין נידונים בהשג יד:
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:13:1.english: And [the Gemara] challenges: Affordability is [stated] regarding one who valuates - And not regarding one who vows, for one who says, “My value is upon me,” is not judged according to affordability; rather, he must give everything when he is able. As we say in the chapter [entitled] “HaOmer Mishkali Alai” (below, Arakhin 20a): “There is a stringency in vows over valuations, for vows are not judged according to affordability.”

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:13:2.hebrew: ומשני כדכתיב על פי אשר תשיג וגו' - כלומר, האי דקרי למעריך הכא ״נודר״ — דלישנא דקרא נקט:
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:13:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: As it is written: “According to the means,” etc. - That is to say, the fact that [the Mishnah] here calls the one who valuates a “vower” [is] because it adopted the language of the verse.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:14:1.hebrew: השנים בנערך ולא בנידר - דהאומר: ״דמי פלוני עלי״, אין נידון לפי מדת שנים, אלא כפי שאותו פלוני נמכר בשוק:
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:14:1.english: The years [are determined] by the one valuated and not by the subject of a vow - For one who says: “The value of so-and-so is upon me” is not assessed according to the measure of years [of age], but rather according to what that so-and-so is sold for in the marketplace.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:16:1.english: And even though his vower is wealthy - [This is asked] in astonishment. “His vower” is the one who said, “The offering of a leper is upon me.”

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:17:1.hebrew: דלמא עליה - דמצורע חס רחמנא אדלות, אבל אמדירו לא, ואע"ג דהוי עני:
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:17:1.english: Perhaps on him - [That is,] on the leper the Merciful One had compassion regarding poverty, but on the one who vows for him, [He did] not, even though he is poor.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:1:1.english: A calamity awaits him - For one over whom forty days have passed without suffering.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:20:1.english: What is [the meaning of] “But with regard to offerings that is not so” - Behold, with regard to offerings as well, you follow the one who vows.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:2:1.english: Because of the rebuke - For He would rebuke them for their actions.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:3:1.english: What is [the meaning of] that which is written: “This is the generation of them that seek after Him” - For it compares the generation to its seekers [i.e., its leaders].

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:4:1.english: For goodness - With regard to piety.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:5:1.hebrew: מאי שנא דכתיב ביהויקים וצדקיהו בראשית? לפי שביקש הקב"ה להפוך מעשה בראשית בימיהם:
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:5:1.english: Why is it different that it is written concerning Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, "In the beginning"? Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to overturn the work of Creation in their days.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:9:1.hebrew: השג יד בנודר - תורת דין השג יד — שהעני נידון בערכין לפי השג ידו, כדכתיב: ״ואם מך הוא מערכך״ — בתר נודר אזלינן, ולא בתר נידר, כדמפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:9:1.english: Means [is determined] by the vower - The rule governing the law of means — that a poor person is judged in valuations according to his means, as it is written: “And if he is too poor for your valuation” — [is that] we follow the vower, and not the one vowed for, as [the Mishnah] explains below.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:9:2.hebrew: והשנים בנידר - כדמפרש לקמן: ילד שהעריך זקן — נותן ערך זקן, דלא אזלינן בתר שנים דידיה דנודר, דהא לא אמר: "ערכי עלי", אלא: "ערך פלוני עלי". וערך זקן — מבן ששים ומעלה — פחות מערך ילד:
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:9:2.english: And the years [are determined] by the one vowed - As explained below: A youth who evaluated an elderly person gives the valuation of an elderly person, for we do not follow the years of the vower himself, for he did not say, "My valuation is upon me," but rather, "The valuation of so-and-so is upon me." And the valuation of an elderly person — from sixty years old and above — is less than the valuation of a youth.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:9:3.hebrew: והערכין בנערך - קצב הערך דזכר ונקבה בתר נערך אזיל, ולא בתר מעריך, כדמפרש לקמן: איש שהעריך אשה, דאמר ״ערך פלונית עלי״ — נותן ערך הנערך:
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:9:3.english: And the valuations [depend on] the one evaluated - The fixed rate of the valuation of a male and a female follows the one evaluated, and not the evaluator, as is explained below: A man who evaluated a woman, who said, "The valuation of so-and-so is upon me" — gives the valuation of the one evaluated.

Rashi on Arakhin 17a:9:4.hebrew: בזמן הערך - כדמפרש לקמן, שאם העריך עצמו פחות מבן עשרים — דהוי ערך קטן — וקודם נתינתו נעשה בן עשרים, אינו נותן אלא כשעה שהעריך תחילה:
Rashi on Arakhin 17a:9:4.english: At the time of the valuation - As it explains below, that if one valuated himself [when he was] less than twenty years old — which is a smaller valuation — and before giving [it] he became twenty years old, he gives only according to [the valuation of] the time that he originally valuated.

Tosafot on Arakhin 17a:10:1.english: "How so? A destitute person who valuated a wealthy person, etc." - (Rashi explained [this]) earlier (Arakhin 7b), in the chapter "Ein Ne'erakhin Pahot," etc.

Tosafot on Arakhin 17a:13:1.hebrew: השג יד בנודר במעריך הוא - פי': במעריך דוקא, לא בנודר — כדקאמרי' לקמן בהאומר משקלי (ערכין דף כ.): "חומר בנדרים מבערכין, שהנדרים חלים על הבהמה ועוף ואין נידונין בהשג יד, מה שאין כן בערכין" (והוא למעוטי מצורע עשיר):
Tosafot on Arakhin 17a:13:1.english: "Affordability [is determined] by the vower" — it is [stated] regarding one who valuates - Explanation: Specifically regarding one who valuates, not regarding one who vows — as we say below in [the chapter entitled] "HaOmer Mishkali" (Arakhin 20a): "There is a stringency in vows over valuations, for vows take effect upon animals and birds, and they are not judged according to affordability, which is not the case with valuations" (and [the word] "he" is to exclude a wealthy leper).

Tosafot on Arakhin 17a:15:1.hebrew: השג יד בנודר כיצד עני שהעריך את העשיר נותן ערך עני - מפי הר"ר מנחם מיאונ"י: כגון עשיר שאמר "ערכי עלי", ושמע עני ואמר "זה עלי" — נותן ערך עני. "אבל בקרבנות אינו כן: הרי שאמר קרבן של מצורע זה עלי כו'" — אהא פליג רבי ואומר: עשיר שאמר "ערכי עלי", ושמע עני ואומר "מה שאמר זה עלי" — נותן ערך עשיר, כמו בקרבנות. וכן משמע פי' דמתני':
Tosafot on Arakhin 17a:15:1.english: "Affordability [depends] on the vower; how so? A poor person who valuated a wealthy person gives the valuation of a poor person" - [Taught] from the mouth of our teacher, Rabbi Menachem of Joigny: For example, a wealthy person who said, "My valuation is upon me," and a poor person heard and said, "This is upon me" — he gives the valuation of a poor person. "But with regard to offerings, that is not so: for [if] one said, 'The offering of this leper is upon me,' etc." — regarding this, Rabbi disagrees and says: A wealthy person who said, "My valuation is upon me," and a poor person heard and says, "Whatever this one said is upon me" — he gives the valuation of a wealthy person, just as with offerings. And so indicates the explanation of the Mishnah.

Tosafot on Arakhin 17a:19:1.hebrew: אבל מדירו עשיר מאי הכי נמי דמייתי בעשירות א"ה מאי אבל בקרבנות אינו כן - והלא בקרבנות כמו כן הדין, שאם אמר עשיר: "קרבנות של מצורע עני זה עלי", מביא קרבן עשיר; וא"כ, מאי חילוק יש בקרבנות לערכין? ומשני: "אחדא", פי' אמצורע עשיר ומדירו עני; דאילו גבי מצורע, אם אמר עני: "קרבן של מצורע עשיר זה עלי", נותן ערך עשיר, דלא אזלינן בתר הנודר; ובערכין אזלינן בתר הנודר, דאילו אמר עשיר: "ערכי עלי", ושמע עני [ואמר]: "מה שאמר זה עלי", נותן ערך עני, דאזלינן בתר הנודר; ומש"ה איצטריך "הוא" למעוטי גביה, דלא אזלינן בתר נודר כמו בערכין. ולרבי, דאמר: ערכין וקרבן שוין בדין זה, אם כן לא איצטריך "הוא" למעוטי מצורע עשיר שמדירו עני דנותן ערך עשיר, שהרי גבי ערכין כן הדין; אלא איצטריך "הוא" למעוטי מצורע עני ומדירו עשיר, דס"ד: הואיל ורבי בתר חיובא דגברא אזיל, ה"נ ניזיל בתר חיובא דגברא ונייתי קרבן עני — קמ"ל דלא. אבל לרבנן, לא איצטריך "הוא" למעוטי מצורע עני ומדירו עשיר, דהואיל דבערכין אזלינן בתר נודר, פשיטא דבמצורע נמי אזלינן בתר נודר, ולא איצטריך "הוא" להכי, כדפי'. וכן פירש רש"י, וכי דייקינן בסוגיא דשמעתין כן הוא. אבל צריך עיון: לרבי, דמדמה אמר העשיר "ערכי עלי" לקרבנות דמצורע עשיר, דעני הנודר בעי לאיתויי קרבן עשיר — והיינו דוקא כשאמר העני: "הרי עלי קרבנות מצורע זה לפוטרו" — ואם אמר כן בערכין, מאי טעמא דרבנן? כיון שאמר: "הרי מה שאמר זה עלי לפוטרו", אם כן נדר בהדיא חמשים סלעים, ואיך נפטר בערך עני:
Tosafot on Arakhin 17a:19:1.english: "But if the one who vows for him is wealthy, what [is the halakha]? Is it indeed so that he brings [the offering brought] in wealth? If so, what is [the meaning of] 'but with regard to offerings it is not so'?" - Yet is not the law in [the case of] offerings likewise, that if a wealthy person said, "The offerings of this poor leper are upon me," he brings the offering of a wealthy person? And if so, what difference is there between offerings and valuations? And [the Gemara] answers: "[The distinction applies to only] one [case]" — meaning, to [the case of] a wealthy leper and the one vowing for him is poor. For regarding a leper, if a poor person said, "The offering of this wealthy leper is upon me," he gives [the assessment of] a wealthy person, because we do not follow the vower; whereas in valuations we follow the vower, for if a wealthy person said, "My valuation is upon me," and a poor person heard and [said], "What this one said is upon me," he gives the valuation of a poor person, because we follow the vower. And that is why [the word] "he" [in "And if he is poor"] was needed to exclude in his case, that we do not follow the vower as [we do] in valuations. And according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who says that valuations and offerings are identical in this law, if so, "he" was not needed to exclude a wealthy leper whose vower is poor, that he gives [the assessment of] a wealthy person, for regarding valuations that is indeed the law; rather, "he" was needed to exclude a poor leper whose vower is wealthy, for it might enter your mind to say: Since Rabbi follows the obligation of the [original] person, here too let us follow the obligation of the [original] person and let him bring the offering of a poor person; [the verse] therefore teaches us that this is not so. However, according to the Rabbis, "he" was not needed to exclude a poor leper whose vower is wealthy, for since in valuations we follow the vower, it is obvious that in [the case of] a leper as well we follow the vower, and "he" was not needed for this, as explained. And so Rashi explained, and when we examine the sugya of our passage closely, so it is. However, it requires further study: According to Rabbi, who compares [the case where] the wealthy person said, "My valuation is upon me," to the offerings of a wealthy leper, where the poor vower must bring the offering of a wealthy person — and that is specifically when the poor person said: "Behold, the offerings of this leper are upon me to discharge him" — if he said so in valuations, what is the reasoning of the Rabbis? Since he said, "Behold, what this one said is upon me to discharge him," if so, he explicitly vowed fifty selas, and how can he be discharged with the valuation of a poor person?

Tosafot on Arakhin 17a:9:1.hebrew: השג יד בנודר והשנים בנידר והערכין בנערך - תימה: אמאי לא ערבינהו בהדי הדדי, וליתני "השנים והערכין בנערך"? ועוד תימ': אמאי לא תני "זכר נותן ערך נקבה", ולא איצטריך לקמן לומר "הערכי' בנערך" כו':
Tosafot on Arakhin 17a:9:1.english: "Affordability [is determined] by the one who vows, and the years by the subject of the vow, and the valuations by the one valuated" - It is puzzling: Why did [the Tanna] not combine them together, and let it teach: "The years and the valuations [are determined] by the one valuated"? And furthermore, it is puzzling: Why did [the Tanna] not teach: "A male gives the valuation of a female," and it would not have been necessary later to say: "The valuations [are determined] by the one valuated," etc.?
